text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Bowing to mounting pressure, the goverment has decided to use the T1-44 vaccine on a trial basis to fight lung disease among cattle in the north of the country. The vaccine has been recommended by the U.N. Food and Agricultural Organisation and approved by the Pan-African Veterinary Vaccine Centre.

- New security measures introduced at Windhoek international airport at the weekend have caused overcrowding and unhappiness among travellers, airline crews and those accompanying passengers to the airport.

- The Ministry of Agriculture, Water and Rural Development has appointed a team of experts to probe an alleged drought relief aid scam. Up to 30 million dollars went missing in the past year. Questions are being raised about what has happened to a report on a previous investigation on the same issue.
